source.rule: System.BSID names another defined system; the variant inherits that system's items, including through a second-level BSID chain if the installed converter accepts it. An undefined BSID is invalid. BSID is a static system type relationship, distinct from CBSID mission reconfiguration.

configuration.first_variant: TEACH-VAR-ADD with BSID TEACH-AIR-01 and TEACH-LRU-ADD
configuration.deployed: TEACH-VAR-GRAND in TEACH-UNIT and TEACH-AIR-01 in TEACH-BASE-UNIT

exact_delta: Both arms add one System row and matching SystemRepair row for TEACH-VAR-GRAND, switch the existing variant deployment to GRAND, and change ProblemDescription. The invalid arm differs from the valid arm only in grandchild System.BSID TEACH-VAR-ADD -> TEACH-NO-SUCH and description. Item, ItemStructure, Unit, Operations, stock, mission, seed and report-control rows remain identical to accepted G03.var03.
pre_run_hypotheses: For valid grandchild, the native event path should expose an inherited TEACH-LRU-ADD failure under deployed TEACH-VAR-GRAND, followed by local replacement and item repair, while the separately deployed zero-rate base succeeds on its own missions. The extra BSID level may alter seed-1 timing; no exact failure timestamp is prespecified.

For invalid-reference, import or conversion should reject the undefined BSID with an explicit diagnostic naming the reference or System row. Record the actual error code/phase; a four-byte or absent SXO and no report are negative evidence, not a successful simulation.
native_acceptance: Each arm uses a unique guarded session-0 SSH run ID, host-wide mutex, GUI PID13340 checks, registry restoration and frozen source/raw seals.

Valid arm: exact populated-table roundtrip, zero converter errors/notes and reviewed warnings, nonempty SXO/log/report, separate base/grandchild mission identities, inherited added-LRU failure/replacement/repair if exposed, report and terminal reconciliation.

Invalid arm: source-level one-reference delta, exact native roundtrip if import succeeds, explicit native rejection at import or conversion, no valid behavioral report, and preserved diagnostic output and exit state.
Separate read-only reviewer replays both arms and raw seals independently of author validation.
diagnostic_gate: If valid chain is rejected or lacks an observable inherited added-LRU path, retain the run as diagnostic and revise under a new candidate version/run ID. If invalid arm is accepted, retain it as a counterexample and do not publish the expected rejection claim without a new contract and run ID.
limits: One two-level BSID chain, one undefined-reference comparator, one seed and one replication; no arbitrary-depth or cycle behavior claim.
No CBSID runtime conversion, GUI visual, alternate failure rates, population inference or cross-engine claim. Aggregate reports do not identify per-unit events.
